blind_comparisons.not_possible_reason: M13 requires eight top-down orthographic renders of settlement PLANS with labels stripped. Round 2 draws no settlement plan: settlement.buildings reaches the door table and a .length and nothing else. The pack's subject does not exist for this round's work. Round 3, in flight in my snapshot, may make it possible for the first time.

ar1.not_applicable_reason: W1-04 ships no combat mechanic. This round adds room geometry, NPC positions and outdoor posts, none of which CombatSystem reads; interiors carry no collision set, so a room cannot change a fight by being in the way.

checks.observed: STRUCTURAL, NOT RE-MEASURED. Round 1 measured the census properly (0 map markers, 0 routes drawn, six-element HUD at 2.05% coverage, openMenu('map') refusing with the S35 text). This round adds render/interior.js, NPC positions and outdoor posts and no HUD surface; the door prompt is still sim.door, a diegetic reach state. The re-measurement is section 4 of tools/world/critic-w1-04-r2b.mjs and it did not run. A successor should take it: a room the renderer now furnishes is exactly where an objective marker would appear first.

ar3.note: The crossings this piece carries are W1-15's and it did not build them: an owner makes taking a thing a crime, a lock tier gates on Security and Agility, and shop hours now derive from isOpenNow() so a door refuses with words at the wrong hour. The crossing this round SHOULD have created is the one it did not: a room's declared lamps deciding whether you can be seen in it. LightField.addSource() has exactly one caller in game/src and it is the harness verb, so a shrine lit by eleven lamps and a smithy lit by none are the same darkness to every guard in Argonia.

GAP-W1-settlement-has-no-outside: 202 buildings still have no exterior geometry in round 2's own work; the eight architecture kits are visible only from indoors.
GAP-W1-interior-lights-unread-by-detection: 827 authored lights are drawn and none reaches LightField (RI-MTH07).
GAP-W1-unique-items-respawn-on-re-entry: sim.world.itemsTaken has no consumer, so every one of 83 unique items can be taken again on every re-entry.
One third of the builder's headline claim 1 is vacuous: exterior_restored_on_exit reads 115 in BOTH arms of its own control.

biggest_gap.what: Round 2 built the inside of 115 buildings and none of the outside of 202. settlement.buildings is read at exactly two sites in game/src: the door table at sim/settlement.js:52 and a .length at engine.js:7749. Each town declares 8-10 bespoke architecture meshes and one silhouette element; 4 per town have a builder (32 of 69) and every one of the 32 is placed INSIDE a room. The 260 townspeople this round put outdoors stand on bare terrain and VP04 is a picture of ground.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: RI-WLD13 §2's sentence for it predates the piece: 'the difference between a settlement of buildings and a settlement of building-shaped doors'. From the player's chair, eight towns with no buildings is a larger absence than any interior defect this round fixed.
biggest_gap.in_flight: W1-04 ROUND 3 is already working on this and its code is in my snapshot: game/src/world/province.js gained 177 lines and game/src/render/exterior.js appeared while I was measuring. I have not measured any of it and this verdict does not grade it. The gap is stated so round 3 has a bar rather than a self-report.

remedy.action: Draw the settlement from settlement.buildings: a mesh per building placed at its offset_m and yaw_deg, drawn from that town architecture_kit.meshes, with the door table already in place as the entry points. Give the draw call a cut arm so the before-picture can be produced on demand.
acceptance: A probe standing at each of the eight settlement centres and reading the SCENE GRAPH reports >= 8 building meshes drawn per town and 202 of 202 across the province, with a --control arm that cuts the draw call and reports 0; the two arms must differ.
Removing five buildings from one settlement's `buildings` list changes the drawn count by five and restores when put back; perturbing architecture_kit.meshes changes which meshes appear.
A pixel sweep of one fixed camera pose at all eight town centres returns 8 distinct images; the control arm returns 1.
VP04-settlement-street contains a building, and the verdict states plainly whether a capture through VP04 may be cited as evidence of a settlement.

other_gaps.what: 827 lights are declared across the 115 interior records and this round drew them. LightField.addSource() — the only way a light enters the stealth detection model — has exactly one caller in the whole of game/src and it is the harness verb addLightSource (harness/api.js:2064). 11 rooms declare zero lights and 37 declare seven, and to the model that decides whether a guard can see you they are the same room.

remedy.action: Register each room's declared lights[] with sim.stealth.light as LightField sources when _applyCell() furnishes the interior, and clear them on leaving. The world positions are already computed by buildInterior().
acceptance: entering a room registers its lights[] as LightField sources
getLightAt() at the same point in a ten-lamp room and a no-lamp room returns different values
snuffing one declared lamp changes visibilityAt() at a point near it
a control that skips the registration reproduces the current reading on both rooms

other_gaps.what: Engine._furnishInterior() splices its own props out of sim.props on leaving (engine.js:4336-4340) and re-spawns them on returning; Engine.spawnProp() always sets taken:false and its duplicate guard at :1931 cannot fire because the old object is already gone. sim.world.itemsTaken records every take, is serialised, is restored and is exposed to the harness, and nothing reads it to suppress a respawn. 83 rooms declare a unique item.

remedy.action: Have _furnishInterior() consult sim.world.itemsTaken before spawning, and spawn with taken:true (or not at all) for an eid already in it.
acceptance: taking a room's unique item and re-entering leaves the pedestal empty, across a save and load
a control that ignores itemsTaken puts it back

other_gaps.what: _furnishInterior() spawns a room's documents with readable and readable_book set; save/state.js serialises props without either field and rehydrates them with readable:null (state.js:730). Inside one session this is masked by the delete-and-respawn; on a fresh engine _interiorProps is empty, nothing is deleted, and spawnProp() returns the stale object. Props have no makeNPC and no durable-field census.

remedy.action: Serialise and read back prop.readable and prop.readable_book, and add the prop field set to save-manifest.json so getDurableFieldCensus() fails loudly on the next omission.
acceptance: a save taken inside a room and loaded on a fresh engine returns listEntities() rows whose readable and readable_book match the pre-save rows
the prop field set is added to game/data/save-manifest.json and checked by getDurableFieldCensus()

other_gaps.what: The round-1 verdict names tools/world/critic-w1-04-r1b.mjs and critic-w1-04-r1c.mjs as the re-measurement path for both its acceptance numbers. Both call launchGame({timeout,width,height}) without spreading args, so neither can be pointed at anything but the live working tree. On a tree that moves every few minutes they cannot produce a stamped number.

remedy.action: Spread args into launchGame in both so --entry works, and re-run each against a frozen snapshot twice to show the number is stable.
acceptance: both spread args into launchGame and accept --entry
a run against a frozen snapshot reproduces its own number twice

corpus_extended.what: RI-WLD13 N1 (footprint containment) is vacuous by construction and this round did not change that: 115 of 115 interiors declare continuity.exterior_footprint_m and on 115 of 115 the bounds_m span equals it exactly. The generator defines the interior's bounds AS the footprint it is checked against.

The round-1 acceptance bar of '>= 100 distinct images over 115 interiors' is not well-formed. The 115 records admit only 94 distinct build-relevant contents, so a sweep can exceed 94 only by counting the hashStr(rec.id) arrangement jitter in buildInterior() — different placements of identical furniture in identically-sized rooms. Restate as: >= 90 distinct images with the room-builder-cut control arm at <= 3.

self_audit.self_audit_note: Four false entries and all four are stated in the verdict rather than worked around. (1) judged_output_not_source is FALSE for the central question: neither browser arm completed, so the blocker's closure is judged from source and from the builder's own artifact, not from a run I took. That is the weakest part of this verdict and I say so in §2, §3 and §4 rather than dressing it up. (2) ran_every_assigned_method is false for the same reason, and additionally the AR-2 census was not re-measured. (3) blind_done_where_required is false: RI-WLD03's M13 is not_possible for round 2's own work because there is no settlement plan to render. (4) I made one offline error and corrected it in the verdict rather than quietly: I first reported RI-WLD13 N1 as 'absent' having grepped a top-level field that lives under continuity; re-measured, it is 115 of 115 and vacuous, exactly as round 1 said. Everything I DID measure — the duplicate-content census, the kit-mesh coverage, the light-field caller count, the prop and area distributions, M14, M15, R2, the property-zone census, the collision-cell census, and the two frames — was measured by me, offline, over the frozen snapshot, and re-verified against it after the tree moved.
